title: Posterior-quantile drafts: the acceptance-optimal draft under known quantization noise (speculative decoding)
stage: theory+method; prior-art screened (the TV first-order law itself is preempted, so the claim is narrowed to the draft-optimality theorem)
hypothesis: Setup: a quantized self-draft sees noisy logits z+delta with heteroscedastic per-token noise. Claim: the draft maximizing expected acceptance is the per-token posterior quantile of p(x), q*(x) proportional to p_hat(x)*exp(-z_lambda*s_x), where s_x is the delta-method std of log p(x). This is a first-order correction, unlike the -sigma^2/2 mean fix or a global temperature, and it is exactly zero under homoscedastic noise. Prediction: on W2/W3/KV2 self-drafts it raises mean accepted length by at least 2% over the best-temperature p_hat.
gap_evidence: Acceptance = 1 - TV is already used as a metric of the quantized model: 2610.00694 (l.36: TV predicts vLLM greedy acceptance within 1.1-2.4%) and 2605.02404 (l.302-307, EAR). Neither shapes the draft given the noise. The 2605.26266 and 2608.14191 corrections target the mean (KL/MSE), not TV. 2610.10411 optimizes drafters without observation noise. arXiv queries for an optimal draft under noise or posterior returned 0 hits.
math_core: Theorem (provable). Phi(q) = E sum_x min(P(x), q(x)) is concave, with dPhi/dq(x) = Pr[P(x) > q(x)]. KKT gives Pr[P(x) > q*(x)] = lambda on the support, so q*(x) = F_x^{-1}(1 - lambda). Corollary: q* = p_hat iff s_x is constant. Greedy targets: propose argmax_x Pr[x = argmax z | z_hat]. Assumptions: Gaussian logit noise with known per-token variance (estimated offline from paired logits), flat prior, continuous marginals. A joint (draft bits, gamma) optimum also follows.
decisive_experiment: Target: Llama-3.1-8B / Qwen3-8B in BF16. Drafts: the same model at W3 GPTQ, W2 QTIP, and KIVI-2 KV. Estimate sigma_x on 512 calibration sequences. Tasks: MT-Bench, GSM8K, HumanEval at T in {0, 0.7}, gamma in {3, 5}. Arms: p_hat, best global temperature, -sigma^2/2 correction, posterior quantile. Cost: 2-4 GPU-days. Fails if the quantile draft gains under 2% accepted length over best-temperature p_hat at both W3 and W2, or if a global temperature reproduces the gain.
nearest_papers: 2610.00694 and 2605.02404: measure TV/acceptance as fidelity; they do not optimize the draft. QSpec/Quasar 2603.01399 and SpecQuant 2609.21704: systems only. 2605.26266: second-order mean-bias correction (KL-motivated); this idea is first-order and quantile-based. FlexDraft 2605.20022: bonus-token calibration, no noise posterior.

title: Winner's curse in quantized-key selection: empirical-Bayes ranking for sparse attention, eviction and recompute selection
stage: theory+method; prior-art screened
hypothesis: Setup: tokens are selected by noisy quantized scores s_hat_i = s_i + delta_i (FP8 lightning-style indexers, Quest/RaBitQ/self-indexing top-k, H2O eviction on quantized K, deviation-guided recompute), with heteroscedastic noise sigma_i. Claim: ranking by s_hat over-selects high-noise tokens and loses attention mass. Ranking by posterior expected mass, m_i + v_i/2 under a per-query empirical-Bayes prior, recovers it. Neither an unbiased score estimator nor a Hadamard rotation removes this bias.
gap_evidence: RaBitQCache 2606.31519 (l.23, l.113) offers an unbiased score estimator as the fix for biased proxies, but unbiased estimation does not give unbiased top-k selection. Fathom 2609.17652 uses score variance only to set read depth and still ranks by the estimate. BreadthKV 2610.05685: an oracle keeping 10% of tokens still loses about 13% of mass, so selection errors cost mass directly. Searches for winner's curse, shrinkage, or empirical Bayes in KV/sparse attention found none.
math_core: Theorem (exact). Assume s_i | s_hat_i ~ N(m_i, v_i) independently, where m_i = (tau^2 s_hat_i + sigma_i^2 mu)/(tau^2 + sigma_i^2) and v_i = tau^2 sigma_i^2/(tau^2 + sigma_i^2). Then the size-k set maximizing E sum_S e^{s_i} is the top-k by m_i + v_i/2. Corollaries: (1) ranking by s_hat is optimal iff sigma_i is constant; (2) the selected-token bias is E[s - s_hat | s_hat] = -sigma_i^2 (s_hat - mu)/(tau^2 + sigma_i^2); (3) the mass lost by naive ranking is a closed-form sum over swapped pairs. Assumptions: Gaussian per-query prior fitted by empirical Bayes; independent noise; sigma_i known from stored scales.
decisive_experiment: Models and tasks: Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B on RULER/LongBench at 32-128K. Selection keys: 1/2/4-bit (KIVI per-channel, per-token INT, RaBitQ 1-bit), for page and token top-k at 1-10% budgets. Arms: s_hat, EB m+v/2, flat-prior s_hat+sigma^2/2. Measure captured exact mass, oracle recall, and accuracy. Cost: 3-5 GPU-days. Fails if EB captures less than 1 pp more mass than naive ranking everywhere, or if the gain is uncorrelated with the dispersion of sigma_i.
nearest_papers: RaBitQCache 2606.31519: unbiased estimator, no selection-bias analysis. Self-Indexing KVCache 2603.14224/2609.13205, PQ-HSA 2609.33746, Fathom 2609.17652, KVBoost 2608.21362, Quest/ZipCache: all rank by point estimates. The DeepSeek-V3.2 indexer precision is recalled from its tech report, not verified this session.

title: Fan-out-aware precision: a bit's value scales with coherent read fan-out (prefix caching, CLA/MLA sharing, SWA vs global, elastic downgrade)
stage: theory+method; prior-art screened
hypothesis: Claim: the marginal value of a bit in a cached tensor is set by the Gram of its read-Jacobians, i.e. its coherent fan-out. At equal bytes this implies: (1) a prefix shared by N requests/samples should get about +1/2 log2(N_coh) bits over per-request suffixes; (2) SWA-layer KV should get 1/2 log2(T_rem/W) fewer bits than global-layer KV; (3) under memory pressure, requests near completion should be downgraded first. Independent per-token errors are averaged by attention; only coherent reuse amplifies them. This would explain Mix-Quant's prefill redundancy.
gap_evidence: Mix-Quant 2605.20315 finds prefill-side quantization 'substantially redundant', which looks inconsistent with a fan-out view; nobody has resolved this. MorphServe 2506.02006 and DPS 2609.34380 change precision under load without a per-tensor value rule. Block-GTQ 2606.24033 Sec. 7 lists batched serving as open. ReadKV 2610.11245 and OSCAR 2605.17757 allocate within one request. No sharing-aware allocation was found.
math_core: Lemma (provable). A cached error e read through maps a_r J_r gives output error E||sum_r a_r J_r e||^2 = tr(G Sigma_e), with G = (sum_r a_r J_r)^T (sum_r a_r J_r). This lies between the incoherent value sum_r ||a_r J_r||^2 and the coherent value (sum_r ||a_r J_r||)^2. Theorem: reverse water-filling with storage multiplicity c_j and weight w_j = tr(G_j)/d_j gives b_j = 1/2 log2(w_j/(lambda c_j)). Assumptions: high-rate quantization, independent errors across entries, first-order linearization.
decisive_experiment: Models: Qwen3-8B / Llama-3.1-8B. (a) Shared prefix with N in {1, 8, 32} samples on GSM8K/MATH self-consistency: fan-out vs uniform bit split at equal bytes. (b) Gemma-3: local vs global KV bit split. (c) Measure tr(G) coherence with JVPs. Cost: about 1 GPU-week. Fails if the gain over uniform is under 0.5 pt (or KL-equivalent) at N=32, the SWA/global split gives nothing, or coherence does not rank the gains.

title: Common-mode quantization error defeats self-consistency; lazy prompt-KV quantization fixes it (parallel sampling / test-time scaling)
stage: finding+method; prior-art screened
hypothesis: Claim: quantization error in a shared prompt KV is common-mode across N parallel samples and concentrated in early decode steps. Predictions: (i) the majority@N gap between quantized and FP KV does not shrink with N, and may grow, whereas per-sample independent error at matched per-sample KL does shrink; (ii) keeping the prompt KV in FP only for the first k decode steps (lazy quantization, transient memory) recovers most of the gap.
gap_evidence: Quantized-reasoning studies (2606.00206; 2610.00694 flips/TV) measure per-sample degradation only. Prefix sharing for n>1 sampling is the vLLM/SGLang default, so the common-mode regime is the deployed one. Searches combining quantization with self-consistency/majority/pass@k and correlated/common-mode error found nothing that separates common-mode from idiosyncratic error.
math_core: Proposition (provable). Let per-problem correctness be pi(c + xi_s), with c common and xi_s independent. As N -> inf, majority accuracy -> 1{E_xi pi(c + xi) > 1/2}. The gap is then Pr[sign(pi_FP - 1/2) != sign(pi_bar(c) - 1/2)]: first-order in c, weighted by the density of problems with pi near 1/2. Independent noise enters only through its expectation, at second order. Lemma: the cross-sample logit-error correlation at step t equals the samples' query alignment against the shared Delta K. It decays as samples diverge, which justifies a finite lazy window.
decisive_experiment: Models and tasks: Qwen3-8B and R1-Distill-Qwen-7B on AIME24/25, MATH500, GPQA. Arms: KIVI-2/3 shared prompt KV vs per-sample re-quantization with independent dither seeds at matched KL. N in {1, 4, 16, 64}; lazy window k in {0, 16, 64, 256}. Also measure cross-sample error correlation vs step. Cost: about 1 GPU-week. Fails if, with the shared prompt, the N=64 gap is at most 50% of the N=1 gap AND lazy k=64 recovers under 30% of it.

title: Dispatch vs combine quantization in expert-parallel MoE: common-mode vs independent error (MoE serving)
stage: theory + ablation; prior-art screened
hypothesis: Claim: dispatch error epsilon is shared by all k experts and propagates coherently (sum_e g_e J_e epsilon), while combine errors eta_e are independent and gate-weighted (sum_e g_e^2 sigma^2). With per-expert-output scales handling outliers, combine therefore tolerates about k_eff/rho times more noise, where k_eff = (sum g)^2/sum g^2 and rho is the measured Jacobian coherence. Current practice (FP4/FP8 dispatch, BF16 combine) may have the communication precision inverted.
gap_evidence: 2603.02731 l.234: 'the combine phase retains BF16 accumulation to preserve reduction precision', with no ablation. DeepSeek-V3 also uses FP8 dispatch and BF16 combine (from memory, not re-read). Five queries found no work that quantizes combine or analyzes the dispatch/combine asymmetry. Adjacent: 2610.03741 studies noisy over-the-air MoE aggregation.

Their ratio is governed by rho = ||sum g_e J_e||_F^2 / sum g_e^2 ||J_e||_F^2 and by output dynamic range. Byte-constrained bit allocation between the two streams by reverse water-filling. The outlier effect on combine scales is empirical.

title: Why route-flip harm is at chance: a tie-indifference theorem for quantized MoE serving
stage: theory + measurement; prior-art screened; novelty moderate-low (the smoothing fix already exists)
hypothesis: Claim: quantization-induced route flips occur at near-ties of an approximately loss-calibrated router. Consequences: (1) a flip's first-order loss change has conditional mean about 0, so its sign is unpredictable from router statistics; (2) net route-mediated damage is second order, proportional to sum over flips of g_tie^2 ||E_k(x) - E_{k+1}(x)||_H^2; (3) gate-continuous blending removes the damage, while pinning the FP route cannot recover more than this second-order term.
gap_evidence: 2608.11212 (OLMoE, top-8, norm_topk_prob=False, 4-bit KV) reports: RMF about 0.31; flip detection AUC 0.772; harm-given-flip AUC 0.490 with P(harmful|flip) = 0.572; the normalization convention acts as a damage-magnitude moderator. It calls this 'an empirical barrier, not a theorem'. 2606.19036 gives discontinuity geometry but not loss sign.
math_core: Proposition. Assume near ties that r_k - r_{k+1} = -c E[L(k) - L(k+1) | x] + o(m). Then E[dL | flip at margin m] = O(m) + 1/2 g_tie^2 dE^T H dE. With m ~ sigma_q at flips, the first-order mean vanishes and the second-order term remains. Half theorem, half finding: the calibration assumption must be measured.
decisive_experiment: Models: OLMoE-1B-7B (unnormalized), Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B / Qwen3-30B-A3B (normalized), DeepSeek-V2-Lite. Noise: 4-bit KV and W4A8. Per flip, compute teacher-forced dL, g_tie and JVP-based ||dE||_H; test predictions (1)-(3), including a soft k/k+1 blend. Cost: 3-5 GPU-days. Fails if the second-order term explains R^2 < 0.3 of mean flip damage, or the soft blend recovers under 50% of RMF.

title: Evict or quantize? A closed-form head-wise rule from the attention tail exponent (KV eviction x precision)
stage: theory + policy; prior-art screened, but 2412.12706 was not read in full (risk)
hypothesis: Claim: if sorted attention weights follow p_(i) ~ C i^{-alpha}, then at a fixed byte budget the keep-all-at-low-precision vs evict-at-high-precision decision flips at a critical alpha_c(B/N), with a closed form via Lambert W. A head-wise policy predicted from alpha beats uniform policies at equal bytes and explains the BreadthKV and 'More Tokens, Lower Precision' regimes.

Minimizing f(n) = A n^{2-2alpha} + K 4^{-B/n} gives n* via Lambert W, and keep-all is optimal iff f'(N) <= 0, which defines alpha_c. Provable under the power-law and independent-error model; whether real heads fit it is empirical.

title: Shared-seed stochastic rounding across data-parallel replicas caps 1/P noise averaging; rank-stratified (correlated) dither fix
stage: FP4/FP8 backward + data-parallel gradient reduction (gradient/communication quantization)
hypothesis: If the stochastic-rounding (SR) random numbers come from the same RNG state on every data-parallel (DP) rank, or on every gradient-accumulation micro-batch, the SR errors are positively correlated (rho = 1/2 for uniform residues). The all-reduced gradient's quantization noise then plateaus at about half the single-rank variance instead of decaying as 1/P. Rank-stratified dither (u_r = (pi(r)+U)/P) makes the errors anti-correlated and beats independent SR. The effect concentrates in channels where the activation operand has a nonzero mean.
gap_evidence: No recipe states that SR must be independent across replicas; they only argue per-step unbiasedness: 2509.25149 (SR on gradients), 2505.19115 (SR backward), 2601.22813 Corollary 3.1. Quartet II App. A (txt l.1535-1548) concedes that EDEN needs independently sampled rotations, yet uses the 'same rotation seed' for both tensors (l.546) and 'identical rotations for every rotation group within a tensor for every micro-batch' (l.1544); unbiasedness is checked only empirically on one GPU (Fig. 9). In the adjacent DME literature, correlated quantization (2203.04925, 2401.05518) shows that correlation structure is a first-order design variable. Premise to verify in step 0: whether Megatron/TE seeding makes SR randomness identical across DP ranks.
math_core: Theorem (exact). Let residues f_r ~ iid U(0,1) and SR errors e_r = 1[u_r<f_r] - f_r. With a shared u: Cov(e_r,e_s) = E[min(f_r,f_s)] - E[f_r f_s] = 1/3 - 1/4 = 1/12, against Var = 1/6, so Var(mean over P) = 1/(6P) + (1-1/P)/12, which tends to 1/12 (at most a 2x reduction for any P). With independent u it is 1/(6P); with stratified u it is O(1/P^2). Transfer to Wgrad = sum_t e_t x_t^T with data independent across ranks: the cross-rank covariance is Cov(e) * E[x_k]^2, so the prediction is channel-specific (post-SwiGLU FC2 inputs, massive-activation channels). Assumptions: residues roughly uniform, data independent across ranks.
decisive_experiment: Step 0: inspect the SR RNG in Megatron + Transformer Engine NVFP4 at DP=8 and measure the per-tensor cross-rank error correlation. Then train a 350M model with an NVFP4 SR backward at DP in {8, 32} under shared, independent and stratified seeds (3 seeds each); report the final loss gap and per-channel noise against E[x_k]^2. About 1 GPU-week. Fail if the measured cross-rank correlation is < 0.05 in all tensors, or if shared and independent seeds give no loss difference beyond seed std. In that case only the stratified-dither method survives, as an improvement over independent SR.

title: A6. Quantizing the KL anchor: a quantized reference or teacher model is noisy reward shaping that grows with sequence length
stage: PTQ/QAT -> RL (KL-regularized RLHF, GRPO with KL, on-policy distillation)
hypothesis: Keeping the reference or teacher model in low precision is exactly equivalent to using the FP anchor plus a reward βη, where η = Σ_t[log π_ref^q - log π_ref]. Because sd(βη) grows as √T, a W4 anchor on long chain-of-thought injects reward noise comparable in size to a binary reward. An FP8 anchor is harmless. The mean part of η pushes entropy up.

title: A7. Precision gating with a distribution-free fidelity guarantee: conformal risk control instead of worst-case certificates
stage: Serving x statistics
hypothesis: A cheap score from the low-bit pass decides whether to escalate the request (or the rest of the generation) to high precision. Candidate scores are the token margin, entropy, and WitCert's per-band residual norm. With conformal risk control this guarantees, from a finite calibration sample, that the fraction of answers differing from the FP model is at most α, while minimizing how often requests are escalated. The guarantee still holds at 1-2 bits, where WitCert's worst-case bound is vacuous.

New to prove: (a) a lemma that the loss stays monotone under mid-generation (token-level) escalation, (b) a weighted-conformal extension for covariate shift. The core theorem is borrowed; the contribution is the cross-application and the design of the loss and scores, and this is flagged as a main-track risk.

title: A4. Quantized generators evade zero-shot text detection and strengthen watermark detection: an entropy-KL identity
stage: Serving quantization -> AI-text detection and watermarking
hypothesis: Suppose the detector scores with the FP model while a quantized model generates the text. Then the expected shift of the Fast-DetectGPT and Binoculars statistic is exactly ΔH - KL, so detection gets worse when quantization raises entropy. The same entropy rise increases the expected green-token rate of KGW-style watermarks. The two detection families therefore move in opposite directions.

title: A2. Attention as a reconstruction filter for V: coherent quantization error, subtractive dither, and token-axis noise shaping  [merged with S09: Token-axis noise shaping of the V cache: zero-storage error feedback (KV cache storage)]
stage: Serving (KV cache) x signal processing
hypothesis:
When V-cache errors are correlated across tokens, attention averaging does not reduce them. The correlation comes from near-constant channels, the deadzone (|v| < Δ/2 rounding to 0), and shared group scales. Subtractive dither seeded by a hash of (token, channel) costs zero bytes of storage and makes the output error average down as 1/N_eff. First-order token-axis sigma-delta needs only one O(d) carry per head, so the storage-doubling objection that 2609.39185 raises for SSM state does not apply. Under smooth attention its output error is smaller still.
[FROM S09] Method: write V with first-order error feedback along the token axis, q_i = Q(v_i - u_{i-1}). Effect: the attention output error becomes sum_i u_i (p_i - p_{i+1}) instead of sum_i p_i e_i, shrinking error power by R = sum(dp)^2/sum p^2 (about 1/N for diffuse heads, at most 2x worse for spiky ones). Cost: no storage overhead, since the carry exists only at write time. Predictions: per-head selection by R gives roughly 1/2 to 1 bit of V-equivalent gain at 2 bits; K-side shaping does not help.
gap_evidence:
WitCert 2607.28699 Lemma 2 [notes] uses subtractive dither only as a certification device; the averaging gain is never analyzed. 2605.13810 [abs] covers only unbiasedness and MSE of dithered RHT. 2606.02288 [notes] reports near-constant bias vectors in keys, which are a source of coherent error. Both KV noise-shaping queries (W5, W6) returned no matching paper.
[FROM S09] Error feedback / sigma-delta has been applied only to recurrent states (2609.39185, 2607.23390, 2609.04490) and weights (SDQ-LLM 2510.03275). 2609.39185 l.594-597 notes that sigma-delta for state caches 'doubles the size of a state cache'; that objection does not apply to write-once KV. KV theory assumes white token-wise noise (AATC 2608.14191 Assumption 1). No KV noise-shaping paper was found.
math_core:
E‖Σ p_t e_t‖² = Σ_{t,s} p_t p_s E<e_t, e_s>. (a) Subtractive dither: dΔ²/(12 N_eff). (b) RTN on a deadzone constant channel: error |v|, independent of N_eff, so dither wins exactly when N_eff > Δ²/(12v²). (c) Token-axis sigma-delta: e_t = ε_{t-1} - ε_t, so the variance is (dΔ²/12)Σ(p_{t+1} - p_t)². This is smaller than dither under smooth attention and at most 2x worse under spiky attention. Per-head selection rule: compare Σ(Δp)² with Σp². V only, because K common-mode error is already handled by softmax shift invariance. All of this is provable.
[FROM S09] Proposition (provable; subtractive dither makes the u_i iid with variance sigma^2). With shaping: E||eps_o||^2 = d sigma^2 [sum_i (p_i - p_{i+1})^2 + boundary terms]; without: d sigma^2 sum p_i^2. Order-L shaping replaces the first difference with the L-th difference; its worst-case factor is C(2L, L). Stability: first-order error feedback stays in range with one quantization step of headroom. For K, the logit error is weighted by p_i (v_i - o), and doubling the per-element variance increases softmax flattening, so K shaping is predicted not to help.

Measure per-head output MSE against the predicted law, then LongBench, RULER and GSM8K-CoT decoding. Fails if the correlation between predicted and measured MSE gain is ρ < 0.5, or if task metrics improve by less than 1 point over RTN. About 1 GPU-week.

title: A3. Extreme-value law for long-context retrieval: KV bits needed grow as ½·log₂ ln N with context length  [merged with S05: KV quantization shrinks usable context polynomially, N*_q = (N*_FP)^{1/(1+r)} (long context)]
stage: Long context x KV quantization x statistics (EVT)
hypothesis:
Needle retrieval (argmax or top-k readout) fails when the noisy maximum over N distractor logits exceeds the needle logit. The failure-onset length then follows ln N*(b) = A/(1 + c·4^{-b}). Fitting the law on short contexts should predict where long contexts fail. The same law gives a per-head bit allocation for retrieval heads as a function of the target context length.
[FROM S05] Claim: in retrieval heads, KV logit noise sigma_q^2 inflates the distractor maximum, so the critical context length obeys ln N*_q = ln N*_FP/(1+r), with r = sigma_q^2/sigma_d^2. Consequences: (1) quantization looks lossless far below the native retrieval limit and fails sharply near it, with required bits b(N) diverging as N -> N*_FP; (2) the weight-quantization gap shrinks with position while the KV-quantization gap grows; (3) length-dependent attention temperature cannot fix hard retrieval.
gap_evidence:
WitCert 2607.28699 [notes]: raw fp8 KV scores only 22.8 on hard RULER, and gating recovers it to 79.7. Nothing explains this large fp8 collapse with a length-dependent theory. Block-GTQ 2606.24033 Lemma 2 [notes]: the logit-error bound has no length term. Queries N1-N5 found no length-versus-bits law.
[FROM S05] 2609.22101 Thm 1 proves an Omega(sqrt(log N)) margin requirement against distractors, but has no quantization. WitCert 2607.28699 gives worst-case bounds that are vacuous at 1-2 bits. 2609.04098 reports the NVFP4 gap shrinking with position, while KVarN 2606.03458 reports KV errors accumulating in pseudo-decode; the sign difference is unexplained. Queries for a quantization length law returned 0.
math_core:
Assumptions: distractor logits iid N(μ, s²); noise ε_j iid N(0, σ²) with σ² = Σ_c q_c²Δ_c²/12. By Gumbel extreme-value asymptotics, P(success) -> Φ((s* - μ)/√(s²+σ²) - √(2 ln N)), so ln N* = (s* - μ)²/(2(s²+σ²)). Substituting σ ∝ 2^{-b} gives a closed-form bit requirement. Correlated distractors are handled through an assumed effective sample size. Sum-of-mass readout and its −σ²/2 bias are excluded because that is preempted (2605.26266).
[FROM S05] Theorem (Gaussian EVT, extending the 2609.22101 setting). Needle score mu+m, distractors iid N(mu, sigma_d^2), and iid N(0, sigma_q^2) noise on all scores. Then Pr[retrieve] -> 1 iff m > (1+o(1)) sqrt(2(sigma_d^2 + sigma_q^2) ln N), so ln N* = m^2/(2(sigma_d^2 + sigma_q^2)). Heteroscedastic noise extends via a Gumbel mixture. A temperature beta scales m and both sigmas equally, so it leaves N* unchanged. This is corollary-level; the contribution is the law plus its quantitative test.

Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B-1M; synthetic needle and RULER NIAH; contexts 4K-128K; K at 2/3/4/8 bits and fp8. Fit on 4K-16K and predict the failure onset at 32K-128K. Fails if predicted N* is off by more than 2x, or if accuracy at fixed bits does not decrease monotonically in ln N. About 1 GPU-week.

title: Loop gain of error-feedback rounding: low-rate overload of GPTQ/LDLQ under fixed-rate block scales (with feedback-aware headroom scales)  [merged with P02: Damping is a loop-gain stabilizer: the optimal GPTQ damping depends on bit-width, not only on calibration sample size] [+P09: Overtraining raises the loop gain: the GPTQ-vs-RTN degradation ratio grows with tokens/parameter]
stage: hypothesis + toy numerical evidence (synthetic Hessians, not LLM)
hypothesis:
The GPTQ/LDLQ quantizer sees z_j = w_j + sum_{k<j} e_k U_kj/U_kk, not w_j. Under independent rounding errors, its variance is sigma_w^2 + (Delta^2/12)*g_j^2, with loop gain g_j^2 = sum_{k<j}(U_kj/U_kk)^2. With block scales computed from the original W (INT-g128, NVFP4, MXFP4), overload is controlled by Delta^2*g_j^2/sigma_w^2. At 2-3 bits on coherent (un-rotated) Hessians this produces substantial overload, and the clipped error re-enters the feedback, which erases the advantage of error feedback. Incoherence processing works at 2 bits mainly because it shrinks max g_j^2. Prediction: headroom scales s* = max|w|/(q - kappa*sqrt(g_j^2/12)), or post-SIC block rescaling, recover a large part of the unrotated-vs-RHT gap.
[FROM P02] GPTQ damping lambda has two roles: generalization (2609.31560 Eq. 35, which depends only on the sample size m) and stability (it bounds the loop gain g_j^2, and the right amount grows with the step Delta). Prediction: at fixed m, lambda*(2-bit) >> lambda*(4-bit) on coherent Hessians, so a two-term rule lambda* = max(lambda_gen(m), lambda_stab(b, H)) beats both the default 1% and the 2609.31560 prescription at 2-3 bits.
[FROM P09] Input covariances become more redundant over training (H_jj/D_jj grows), so the GPTQ loop gain g_j^2 rises with training tokens at a fixed LR phase. The RTN/GPTQ damage ratio then rises at 4 bits but falls at 2-3 bits as overload sets in. Part of 'overtrained models quantize worse' is specific to Hessian-based rounding rather than a property of the weights, and the trend should flatten with RHT.

QuIP via 2608.25188 Sec. 7.2: the LDLQ rounder alone gives 123.9 PPL vs 6.33 with incoherence at 2 bits (Llama-2-70B), and the permutation alone is 'worth 74 perplexity'. QTIP 2406.11235 v1-v3: Hessian rounding is 'worse than expected on Llama 3'. Toy result (coherent H, INT2 g128, damping 1e-4): 15.7% of quantizer inputs overload, input-variance inflation 14.3x, proxy 0.152 vs 0.031 at damping 0.01. In a random (incoherent) basis, overload is <=0.1%.

The GPTQ default damping is constant across bit-widths. 2507.18553 Sec. 4.5: min-pivot ordering lowers tr(D) but gains are 'modest', which fits a picture where tr(D) ignores the loop gain. Proposition (exact under subtractive dither/SR; approximate for RTN): with independent zero-mean errors of variance Delta_k^2/12, Var(z_j - w_j) = sum_{k<j}(Delta_k^2/12)(U_kj/U_kk)^2, and by Hoeffding Pr(overload_j) <= 2exp(-(qs-|w_j|)^2/(2Var)). Target theorem (clipped Babai bound): E||(W - W-hat)H^{1/2}||^2 <= (1/12)sum_j D_jj Delta_j^2 + sum_j D_jj E[(|z_j| - qs)_+^2], with the overload term bounded through g_j^2. This is a finite-alphabet extension of 2507.18553 Thm 5. Corollary: the closed-form headroom scale minimizing the bound. The deterministic-RTN case is not provable (errors correlate with w) and is stated as an empirical law.

Under the idea-1 bound and monotonicity of g_j^2 in lambda (true for diagonally dominated H; must be proved or restricted), comparative statics give d lambda*/d Delta > 0. The interaction with the sample-size term is empirical.
